name: Lantern-pattern Squad Drone Kit (SD-1 Wisp, SD-2 Tick, SD-C cradle)

scale.label: 1:56 (30 mm heroic Vigil line)
scale.note: Vehicle-tier ratio: every drone dimension is the in-world size / 56 (17.86 mm per metre), then heroic exaggeration where a feature would not print (see exaggerations).

printer: 8K 7-inch class MSLA, build volume 153.36 x 77.76 x 165 mm (tools/mcpcheck.py PRINTERS)
frame: mm, z up, every part faces -y (its left on +x); Wisp body centre at the origin; Tick, mast and weapon seats at z = 0; cradle and saddle in the Vigil backpack frame (front face y = 0, peg toward -y).

assumptions.decision: Flight stem: a printed 1.6 mm resin stem ships in the kit; every stem socket is a round 1.8 mm glue-fit bore, so a bought 1.6 mm clear acrylic rod fits the same sockets.
A 'landed' Wisp (legs and skids down, no stem socket) is included for objective markers.

The SD-C cradle clips on behind the spine pack: a contoured pack saddle seats over the top and back of the line-standard power pack and carries the standard 2.0 mm D-flat socket; the cradle's 2.0 mm D-flat peg plugs into it (or straight into a figure's pack socket to replace the pack).

Flying Wisps lean forward: the base stem socket is raked 24 deg from a launch pad 9.6 mm behind the centre, so a perpendicular Wisp socket puts the drone in a nose-down forward-flight attitude over the base centre (M4 at 18 deg, pushed to 24 deg in M6).

stem.rod_note: 1.6 mm clear acrylic rod, cut to 27 mm, fits the same sockets

exaggerations: Duct walls 0.85 mm (true scale ~0.1 mm): MSLA unsupported-wall floor 0.6 mm, owner brief >= 0.8 mm.
Wisp arms 1.2 x 0.9 mm, keel spine 0.9 mm, Tick parts >= 0.9 mm everywhere (brief).
Split-chevron lens recesses 0.44 mm wide, about 0.35 mm deep (engraving limit 0.4 mm) so a wash finds them.
Talon carbine (VW-05, tools/armory.py) grown 0.05 mm so its 0.84 mm red-dot clears the Tick's 0.9 mm floor.
Track shoe grooves 0.4 x 0.3 mm on a 0.95 mm pitch (true shoe pitch ~0.1 m = 1.8 mm, halved so the track reads as a track).

catalog.revision_note: resin drone kit: 2 flying Wisps, landed Wisp, Tick + 3 weapon modules, cradle + pack saddle, stems, 32 mm bases
catalog.base: 32 mm round x 3 mm, 5 x 2 mm magnet pocket vented to the rim; stem bases carry a 24 deg raked 1.8 mm stem socket
catalog.description: The Lantern kit every Vigil fireteam carries: the SD-1 Wisp ducted quadcopter (recon, or designator and munition, plus a landed marker), the SD-2 Tick tracked crawler with a periscope mast and swappable Talon carbine, mine-plough or relay-and-smoke modules, and the SD-C cradle that clips a folded Wisp behind a trooper's spine pack.

buildNotes: Wisp: one piece (chevron body, four 0.85 mm-wall ducts, rotors recessed 0.4 mm, chin ball with split-chevron lenses); round 1.8 mm stem socket under the body.
Flight stem: printed 1.6 mm resin, or cut a 1.6 mm clear acrylic rod to 27 mm; it seats 3 mm into the raked base socket and 2 mm into the Wisp.
Tick: hull and tracks in one piece; the periscope mast (1.2 mm D-flat peg) and one weapon module (1.6 mm D-flat peg) plug into the deck.

SD-C: glue the pack saddle over the top and back of a line-standard power pack; the cradle (folded Wisp) plugs into the saddle on the standard 2.0 mm D-flat pack peg, or straight into a figure's pack socket.
Every part prints on supports in the orientation miniature_support_plan picked (print/stl is already in that pose).
catalog.limitations: Procedural SDF sculpt, not a hand sculpt. Printability is a heuristic screen through unified-CAD-MCP, not a test print; print a tolerance coupon for the 0.1 mm glue fits. No STEP: FreeCAD is not installed on the build host, so cad/ holds no assembly STEP (recorded as skipped).

triangle_budget_note: Marched meshes are never decimated: if a part marches over budget the field is re-meshed at a coarser pitch (miniature_mesh_budget rule, triangles ~ 1/pitch^2). 160k keeps >= 3 voxels across every 0.4 mm feature on the small parts and halves the printability-check time; bases keep 250k so the 0.45 mm deck seams stay >= 3 voxels wide.
